notes:
Account snapshot:
- Company: Ironclad Payments Group (global payments processor, heavy PCI scope).
- Want Private VPC deployment in AWS (us-east-1 primary; EU region for EU customers).
- Primary ask: network-level isolation + strong egress controls + CMK/KMS integration + audit log forwarding.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-01-15: initial inbound (marketing SDR) — qualified to AE (Evan).
- 2025-01-22: kickoff call (Fireflies ff_2025-01-22_icpg_vpc-kickoff) — overview of Redwood Private, asked about PrivateLink vs VPC peering.
- 2025-01-29: architecture deep-dive with infra lead (Jack Liu, SecOps) — requested sample route table and SG/NACL patterns.
- 2025-02-03: sent draft VPC reference diagram + isolation patterns (internal review).
- 2025-02-10: security review with SecOps and Legal (ff_2025-02-10_secops-review) — raised KMS key ownership, audit forwarding, retention, and data residency.
- 2025-02-18: POC request submitted: staging VPC with PrivateLink endpoint + customer-managed CMK for token encryption.

Technical / requirements (customer-specified):
- Network: prefer AWS PrivateLink for production; OK to evaluate VPC peering for performance-sensitive routes. Must support static IPs for allowlist.
- Firewall: Security team wants strict SGs + NACL defaults, deny-all egress except to Redwood service endpoints; egress to logging/metrics endpoints (Splunk, Datadog) must be allowed.
- Egress controls: require NAT + proxy chain; no outbound internet from inference subnets except via approved egress.
- IP allowlists: will provide /32 list for control plane management; require support for additional CIDR blocks during rollout.
- Routing: explicit route tables per AZ, no cross-account open routes.
- KMS: customer insists on customer-managed CMK in their AWS account (HSM-backed preferred) with external key policy granting Redwood minimal usage rights. Must show key usage logs.
- Audit logging: forward all API and runtime logs to customer Splunk/S3 with 7-year retention; need proof-of-concept that Redwood can ship audit events (access, model loads, key usage) to their SIEM.
- Data residency: EU data must be pinned to eu-west-1 model replicas; metadata residency controls required.

Security review notes / quotes:
- Jack Liu (SecOps): "Cannot accept shared KMS — must be CMK in our account or we walk."
- Head of Infra: "We need concrete egress proof — show us that tokens never leave the VPC except to your PrivateLink endpoint."
- Legal: DPA redlines on data retention and subprocessors; want SOC2+ISO27001 evidence.

POC scope agreed:
- Build a staging VPC with PrivateLink endpoints + one peered VPC for throughput test.
- Demonstrate CMK integration: Redwood uses customer CMK for token encryption; show CloudTrail key usage events.
- Egress test: lock down subnets and run inference workload demonstrating only allowed egress to Splunk and Redwood control plane via PrivateLink.

Open questions / risks:
- Can Redwood support static outbound IPs for control-plane callbacks? Engineering said may require NAT + EIP in customer account.
- Fallback behavior: customer wants guaranteed local model fallback (EU) if us-east capacity constrains — need confirmed model routing policy.
- SLA negotiation: enterprise SLA + maintenance windows to be discussed.

Next steps (owner: Evan):
- Deliver detailed VPC reference diagram and runbook (by 2025-02-24).
- SE (Priya) to prepare KMS integration runbook and CloudTrail example.
- Schedule SecOps follow-up for technical signoff (target 2025-02-26).
- Legal to receive updated DPA with proposed redlines (in progress).

Quick CRM-style bullets for reps:
- High ARR potential, strong security bar.
- Main win criteria: CMK ownership + demonstrable egress isolation + audit log forwarding.
- Blockers: SecOps signoff, network calendar, DPA finalization.
